title: Distribution & Pairwise Correlations
objective: Assess normality and outliers in performance_rating; compute pairwise correlations of every numeric feature against performance_rating.
required_checks: Test pairwise correlations between all numeric features and performance_rating before modelling
Check distribution of performance_rating for normality and outliers
steps: Load dataset CSV.
Compute Shapiro-Wilk test on performance_rating and report W statistic and p-value.
Identify any performance_rating values beyond mean +/- 3 standard deviations.
Plot histogram and boxplot of performance_rating (save as plots/exp01_performance_dist.png).

Compute Pearson and Spearman correlation of each numeric feature (years_experience, training_hours, team_size, projects_completed, satisfaction_score, commute_minutes, remote_pct) vs performance_rating, with p-values.
Plot bar chart of Pearson correlation coefficients (save as plots/exp01_correlations.png).
Summarise: list any feature with |r| > 0.1 and p < 0.05; otherwise state no significant correlations found.
expected_result: No feature shows a significant correlation with performance_rating; distribution is approximately normal.

title: Salary Band Investigation
objective: Determine whether salary_band acts as an ordinal proxy by examining level frequencies and cross-band feature distributions.
required_checks: Verify salary_band is not a proxy for an ordinal variable by inspecting level frequencies and feature distributions per band
steps: Load dataset CSV.
Compute frequency counts for each salary_band level.
Compute group-wise mean and std of years_experience, training_hours, performance_rating, satisfaction_score per salary_band.
Run Kruskal-Wallis test for performance_rating across salary_band levels; report H statistic and p-value.
Plot boxplot of performance_rating by salary_band, ordered L1-L5 (save as plots/exp02_salary_band.png).
Check for monotonic trend: compute Spearman rank correlation between numeric band rank (1-5) and group mean of each feature.
Summarise: state whether any feature shows a monotonic trend across bands.
expected_result: salary_band levels are roughly balanced and show no monotonic trend in any feature; Kruskal-Wallis p > 0.05.

title: Multicollinearity Assessment
objective: Compute VIF and pairwise correlations among numeric predictors to detect multicollinearity.
required_checks: Assess multicollinearity among predictor features before interpreting regression coefficients
steps: Load dataset CSV.
Select numeric predictor columns (exclude employee_id and performance_rating).
Compute VIF for each predictor using statsmodels variance_inflation_factor.
Compute pairwise Pearson correlation matrix among predictors.
Plot correlation heatmap (save as plots/exp03_vif_heatmap.png).
Flag any VIF > 5 or pairwise |r| > 0.7.
Summarise findings.
expected_result: All VIFs below 5 and no pairwise |r| exceeds 0.7; predictors are independent.

title: Permutation Baseline Test
objective: Compare OLS R-squared on real data against a null distribution from 200 target-shuffled permutations to determine if observed signal exceeds chance.
required_checks: Run a baseline permutation or shuffle test to confirm any observed signal exceeds chance
steps: Load dataset CSV.
Select numeric predictors (exclude employee_id). Target = performance_rating.
Fit OLS regression, record observed R-squared.
Repeat 200 times: shuffle performance_rating, refit OLS, record R-squared.
Compute empirical p-value = (number of permuted R-squared >= observed R-squared) / 200.
Plot histogram of permuted R-squared values with observed R-squared as a vertical line (save as plots/exp04_permutation.png).
Summarise: if p > 0.05, conclude no evidence that the model captures real signal.
expected_result: Observed R-squared falls within the permuted null distribution; empirical p > 0.05.
